summary: Start to see that counting tells you how many things there are.
Say the counting numbers out loud in the right order, with none skipped.
Recognize written numbers, like the ones seen around the room.
Count objects by touching each one once while saying one number for it.
Compare groups of objects using words like more, less and the same.
Count a group to find out how many there are, and say the number.
Use numbers in everyday life, like working out how many cups are needed for snack.
Use order words like first, second and third to say where things are in a line.
Understand that each number stands for an amount, and match numbers to groups.
Start to recognize, name, describe, build and draw flat and solid shapes.
Put together and take apart puzzles that get harder over time.
Tell how shapes are alike or different, such as in size, shape or color.
Show and say where objects are, using words like in, on and under.
Recognize, copy and continue simple patterns made with all kinds of materials.
Line up objects in order by one feature, such as size, from smallest to biggest.
Start to understand time through the order of the day, like snack, circle time and bedtime.
Sort and match real objects by a feature like color, size or shape.
Measure things with hands, feet or blocks, and with real tools like a ruler or tape measure.
Explore what can be measured about things, like weight, length, how much they hold, and temperature.
Start to compare and sort things by length, size or weight, using words like taller or heavier.
Start to show data using real objects, pictures and simple graphs.
Start to compare collected data and say what it shows, like which group has more.
